A genuinely different mechanism from a fixed-value sweep -- adaptive, learned during training, not a hyperparameter search over scalars.

config.hypothesis: PDAOM (arXiv:2304.09176) reconstruction: a pairwise EXPONENTIAL AUC-optimization loss (steeper than BPR's bounded log-sigmoid) combined with per-user HARD-PAIR MINING (hardest positive vs. hardest negative per batch, not BPR's uniform random pair) -- a genuinely different bet than fm_bpr/deepfm_bpr's pairwise loss (tested twice, both plateaued below baseline). Paper reports real GAUC/AUC gains over plain pairwise exponential loss in a production feed-recommendation system. Source paper's PDF text could not be machine-extracted (image-embedded); this is a faithful reconstruction from its abstract-level description plus standard AUC-optimization + batch-hard-mining literature, not a citation of its exact tuned constants.
config.notes: Standalone check (tools/check_pdaom.py). Severe regression, not noise: valid primary 0.5483 (single seed) vs. parent's 0.6035 -- a magnitude far beyond any plausible noise band, no 3-seed re-verification needed to see this is real. Diagnosed with two quick ablations before stopping: max_candidates=2 (0.5764) and max_candidates=1, i.e. NO hard mining, just the exponential loss on a random pair (0.5917) -- still below deepfm_bpr_v1_regularized (0.5980) even with mining fully removed. Clean causal story: BOTH ingredients hurt independently -- the exponential loss shape is less numerically stable than BPR's bounded log-sigmoid for this task (loss barely moves epoch-to-epoch, ~1.003 the whole run, a sign of a weak/unstable gradient signal), and hard-pair mining compounds that instability further by concentrating gradient on extreme/noisy pairs -- a documented failure mode of pure hardest-mining vs. semi-hard mining in the metric-learning literature (e.g. FaceNet, Schroff et al. 2015, moved away from pure hardest mining for exactly this reason). Not pursued further given this diagnostic clarity and that the source paper's exact tuned constants were unavailable to try instead.

config.hypothesis: Replaces 'deepfm_mtl_v1''s main-task BCE with focal loss (Lin et al. 2017) -- a genuinely different lever than any architecture, auxiliary-signal, or MTL-mechanism change already tried: it changes which examples matter during training, not the model or the signal set. Directly motivated by the per-segment diagnosis (P2_FEATURES_AND_RESULTS.md Sec.15), which found ranking quality measurably worse on mid-popularity items specifically -- plain BCE trains every row uniformly regardless of that per-segment difficulty; focal loss's (1-p_t)^gamma modulating factor should automatically reallocate gradient toward harder examples across the dataset. gamma=2.0 (paper default), alpha=0.5 (neutral -- isolates the hard-example effect from class-balance correction, a separate question this dataset's mild ~31-34% imbalance doesn't obviously need). Same fields/k/hidden/l2/aux_weight/aux_heads as the parent, so the loss function is the only variable.

config.hypothesis: Direct follow-up to the ten-refinements-of-deepfm_mtl_v1 pattern (P2 SS10-19): a structurally different lever from a different family entirely. LambdaRank (Burges et al. 2006) weights each within-user (positive, negative) pair by the actual |delta nDCG@5| swapping it would cause, targeting the scored metric directly rather than treating every violated pair equally the way BPR does, or using a metric-agnostic softmax the way the listwise attempt does. Same DeepFM backbone/hyperparameters as deepfm_regularized/deepfm_listwise -- only the loss function differs.

Result: best epoch 2/7 -- validation primary peaks early then steadily WORSENS every epoch after even as training loss keeps falling, the same fast-convergence-to-shallow-optimum shape fm_bpr_default first showed. Third independent confirmation (after FM_BPR, DeepFM_BPR) that pairwise-sampled losses underperform pointwise BCE on this benchmark.

Replaces DeepFM/deepfm_regularized's FM 2nd-order interaction term with a Cross Network (Wang et al. 2020, DCNv2): n_cross_layers stacked explicit-cross layers run in parallel with a plain deep MLP tower, both reading the same flattened embedding. config.hypothesis: Every prior MTL refinement (uncertainty-weighting, PCGrad) changed how much the auxiliary losses count or how their gradients combine with the main task -- never whether the aux heads have enough capacity to extract a clean signal. deepfm_mtl_v1 maps all 4 auxiliary tasks through ONE shared nn.Linear(hidden[-1], 4) -- the same weight matrix for every task, no task-specific nonlinearity. This gives each task its own small private MLP (Linear->ReLU->Linear, head_hidden=32) instead. Same shared trunk/embeddings, main task unchanged -- only the auxiliary heads capacity is the variable being isolated.

config.hypothesis: A genuinely different mechanism from every other lever tried: every prior attempt changed the loss, architecture, training signal, or combined already-trained models, but all still treat embeddings as a pure lookup table learned from scratch via gradient descent. This instead injects collaborative-filtering structure BEFORE training: LightGCN-style (He et al. 2020) 2-layer normalized-adjacency propagation over the train-split user-video is_click=1 graph, used to initialize deepfm_mtl_v1's user_id/video_id embedding rows (rescaled to match the random init's own std) instead of random init. Same architecture/loss/hyperparameters as deepfm_mtl_v1 -- only the embedding INITIALIZATION is the variable being isolated.
